observations: Photo 0 shows a large curved monitor with a dark blue abstract wallpaper, placed on a desk next to a laptop. The monitor has thin bezels and a black frame. The screen displays text like 'RECONNECTION', 'WORLD', 'WITH GOD', etc., suggesting a custom or branded wallpaper.

Photo 1 shows the same monitor from a wider angle, placed on a black desk with a laptop, keyboard, mouse, and other desk accessories. The monitor is positioned behind the laptop, and a second identical monitor is visible on the right, still in its box. The box has the same abstract design and text as the screen.
The monitor appears to be a 34-inch ultrawide curved display, based on its aspect ratio and size relative to the laptop.
No brand or model name is visible on the monitor or its stand in either photo.
The box on the right in photo 1 has the same design as the screen, suggesting it is the original packaging, but no brand or model is readable.
The seller claims 34" WQHD, 100Hz, SRGB 99%, HDR10, and USB-C with 65W — none of these specs are visible in the photos.

claims.evidence: The size and curvature are consistent with a 34-inch curved monitor, but resolution cannot be confirmed from photos. No on-screen display or bezel text confirms WQHD.
Color accuracy and HDR support cannot be verified from photos alone. No calibration data or test patterns are visible.
Refresh rate cannot be confirmed without checking the monitor's settings or specifications. No on-screen display or OSD menu is visible.
No ports are visible on the monitor or its stand. The presence of USB-C and 65W power delivery cannot be confirmed from the photos.

risks.risk: Monitor may not be 34-inch WQHD as claimed
risks.proof: A close-up photo of the monitor's bezel or on-screen display showing the model name and resolution.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as a generic curved monitor without confirmed specs, which may be significantly lower than a true 3440x1440 100Hz model.

risks.risk: Refresh rate may be lower than 100Hz (e.g., 60Hz)
risks.proof: A photo of the monitor's OSD menu showing the refresh rate setting, or a screenshot from the monitor's settings.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as a 60Hz monitor, which is significantly cheaper than 100Hz.

risks.risk: USB-C with 65W may not be present or functional
risks.proof: A photo showing the back or side of the monitor with visible USB-C port and power delivery label, or a test video showing a laptop charging via USB-C.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as a monitor without USB-C or power delivery, which reduces value.

risks.risk: Monitor may be used or damaged (scratches, dead pixels, burn-in)
risks.proof: A close-up photo of the screen under white or black background to check for defects, and a photo of the back and stand for wear.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as used with potential defects, which reduces value.
